decision_journal.decision: Built recoverMissingOhlcvSession() + runOhlcvCandlePresenceGuard() net-new (sibling ALPHA-S1-CANDLE-RECOVER closed false-positive, shipped no code, so its shared primitive never existed). Calendar-aware via vnTradingCalendar's new mostRecentTradingDayOnOrBefore() (bounded 14-day backward walk over isVnTradingDay) — structurally prevents ever treating a weekend/holiday as a missing session. Wired at startup (static import) + trailing inside runOhlcvDailyAggregator itself (checks the PREVIOUS trading day via nowMs-24h, dynamic import to avoid a static circular import back through this same file). Fixed a real arithmetic bug in the architect design doc's illustrative re-aggregation snippet (nowMs must be end-of-VN-session, not midnight+5h, else the afternoon close is silently dropped from the recovered candle) — disclosed in commit message, not a re-architecture. Fail-loud does not invent a new retry ladder: a persistent gap that routes through VPS-relay is escalated by the ALREADY-EXISTING R-5 ladder in handleOhlcvBackfillDone (sibling commit 599f4aee0) once the poller reports back. Commit 1bbc8cead, disjoint file set from the sibling row. Moved in_progress->review, deploy_pending:true, top-level .head synced to next_agent:qa.
decision_journal.what_considered: (A) implement recoverMissingOhlcvSession per the architect's §1 snippet verbatim, including the nowMs=midnight+5h re-aggregation window — REJECTED after a direct unit test (3 ticks spanning the full VN session) showed the aggregator's own window is [vnMidnight(nowMs), nowMs), so +5h truncates capture to the pre-market hours and silently drops the actual session close; would have shipped a recovery path that produces a wrong candle while looking correct. (B) leave the trailing daily-aggregator call site as a static import of ohlcvCandleGuard.ts — REJECTED: creates a 3-node static circular import (ohlcvDailyAggregatorJob -> ohlcvCandleGuard -> recoverMissingOhlcvSession -> ohlcvDailyAggregatorJob); used a dynamic import instead, mirroring the deferred-load idiom ohlcvStartupProbe.ts already uses for the same reason. (C) add a bespoke retry-cap/escalation ladder inside the guard itself for a persistent gap — REJECTED per the task's explicit instruction to reuse the existing ladder, not invent a new one: the VPS-relay branch's ohlcv_backfill_queue insert already flows into the sibling's already-fixed R-5 ladder.
decision_journal.why_change: Architect design (docs/handoffs/ALPHA-S1-architect-design.md §1/§2) is the design authority and was followed for orchestration/branch structure/interfaces verbatim; the one deviation (aggregation-window arithmetic) is a correctness bug-fix within the design's own illustrative code, not a scope or architecture change, and is fully disclosed in the commit message and notebook.

No other row in this table embeds a fenced/multi-line block below it, so no direct precedent existed; chose Option 2 (qa's own flagged safer option) as the spec-compliant fix.

It still requires router-adjudicated dispatch and will not self-start; that is stated on the row and returned to the router as an explicit action. (c) NO history rewrite — concur with the router. Peers are actively committing to shared main; rewriting HEAD under live concurrent writers risks exactly the class of loss we are fixing, and would invalidate peer local refs. decision_journal.what_considered: (A) Accept the risk and record it, per the router's explicit option — REJECTED: three occurrences, two of them inside six minutes, and the third actor performed the documented diligence (`git diff --cached --name-status`) and was swept anyway because a --cached read is a snapshot, not a lock. Accepting risk is only honest where the control is untried; here the control (documentation) has been tried and has measurably failed. (B) Re-scope the EXISTING row and dispatch that instead of minting — REJECTED: its scope is wrong at the root, not merely stale. It targets one agent's flow doc, and the two new occurrences came from the router and cowork-team, which that scope could never reach. Editing it would preserve a per-agent framing that the evidence refutes. Superseded-in-place instead so the occurrence-0 datum survives. (C) next_agent=developer so BOUNDED-1 auto-promotes it — REJECTED despite being the only option that self-dispatches. The candidate mechanisms differ sharply in blast radius, and a fleet-wide hard-reject pre-commit hook chosen by an unattended generic developer via zone-detect's Tier-3 fallback is the specific bad outcome: a misfiring hard-reject blocks every agent and every human on the repo. A design gate is worth the cost of manual dispatch here. (D) Mandate fail-closed on the guard, citing UC-CRITIC-HOOKS-ENFORCEMENT — REJECTED as overreach into design AND as wrong on the merits: fail-closed on a PRE-COMMIT hook IS the fleet-outage risk. The defect that row documents is SILENCE (`2>/dev/null || true` makes a crashed validator look like a pass), not leniency. Encoded the observability requirement as acceptance (3) and left the reject-vs-warn disposition to architect. (E) Rewrite the two mis-attributed commits — REJECTED per (c) above.

decision_journal.why_change: Two corrections to router's evidence, both verified by executing code rather than reading it. FIRST, on (1): router called the fix '~3 lines, helpers already exist' and proposed mirroring the NEWS branch. I ran freshnessSlaChecker directly against the real cadence and that fix is arithmetically insufficient — lastExpectedSbvWindowEnd hardcodes a 10:00Z window end (17:00 VN) while SBV actually publishes ~03:05Z (10:05 VN), so with OFF_HOURS_GRACE_MINUTES=30 there is a constant ~384-min excess the branch arm cannot remove. That also exposed a defect NEITHER of us saw: the already-shipped weekend arm (d71e3f2e2) is broken by the same constant and has never worked at real cadence — it passes only because fixture S-1 uses age=289 against a 1470 threshold when the real weekend age is ~1854. So the row grew from one arm to two arms plus a fixture re-base, and clause (E) was scope-corrected because TC-5d pins the CONFIG FIELD not getSlaThreshold's OUTPUT, meaning it does not block the branch-level fix router proposed — router called it 'the most valuable clause'; it is real but conditional. SECOND, on (3): router claimed the AC7 golden-stdout guard has been dark since a5d079663. It has not — AC7 runs BEFORE the first makeOrchRefHarness() call and I observed both its assertions PASS. What is actually dark is 13 assertions after line 273: FIX-DRAIN-PAYLOADREF (3), ENOBUFS (4), unparseable-loud (6). That correction raised rather than lowered the severity, because unparseable-loud guards 0-byte-file handling — exactly the behaviour under active change in rulings (5) and (6) — which is why the row is P0 despite a one-line fix, and why I added harness-green as a precondition on the step-3 deletion gate.

entries.product_decision: Option (a) chosen: re-enable prediction synthesis on a DAILY cadence by routing digest-predict to a daily prediction sub-flow + a new daily cowork slot, WITHOUT disturbing the Sunday weekly calibration report. backlog.title: PUBLISHED-MARKER LIFECYCLE — one marker-gate skill, publish-state-conditioned immunity; wire into the 6 copy-pasted gates (P0: caused CONFIRMED user-visible MARKET double-publish 2026-07-15 ids 932+933)
backlog.note:
P0-PROMOTED 2026-07-15T20:06Z by po from signal cow-20260715T195545 (CONFIRMED user-visible double publish, MARKET ids 932+933). UMBRELLA — folds FIX-CHEF-PUBLISHED-MARKER-RELEASE + FU-CHEF-MARKER-INFLOW; both set BLOCKED on this row. THEY MUST NOT SHIP INDEPENDENTLY — independent point patches provably OSCILLATE: 07-02 marker released post-publish -> double publish; 07-03 remediation said release-on-every-no-post-exit -> marker LEAKED on silent exit, suppressing legit dishes; 07-15 an agent complied with the 07-03 rule and released after a REAL publish -> double publish again. The two memory lessons feedback_chef_leaks_published_marker_on_silent_exit (release it!) and feedback-chef-releases-published-marker-enables-peer-double-publish (never release it!) are in DIRECT CONTRADICTION and are auto-injected into agent context — so ANY prose-only fix is non-deterministic by construction. ROOT CAUSE (deeper than the release itself): chef.md claims the marker at Step 0.5 line 32, ~650 lines and one full expensive gather/synthesis BEFORE send_telegram. Claiming before the publish decision is what forces a conditional-release rule, and agents get that conditional wrong in BOTH directions. Note the existing UC-CCA-P3 clause mandatory release-on-no-publish is INSUFFICIENT — it encodes the 07-03 half of the pendulum only. REQUIRED INVARIANT (the WHAT — architect/ba own the HOW): marker release-immunity MUST be a function of publish-state, not of agent prose. Publish SUCCEEDED -> marker is an immutable tombstone, TTL is the ONLY expiry path. Publish NOT attempted/failed -> marker must not survive. PO DESIGN RECOMMENDATION (non-binding, architect decides): two-phase gate — (1) early cheap READ-ONLY probe task_list_held(task_id=MARKER_KEY) at Step 0.5 to abort before burning the pipeline, claiming NOTHING so a leak is impossible; (2) task_claim immediately before send_telegram, claimed:false -> EXIT without sending, claimed:true -> send -> NEVER release. Late-claim makes conditional-release logic unnecessary while the early probe preserves the cost optimisation the current early-claim was reaching for. AC-CODE-GATE (assess, do not assume): prose gates have now failed 3x — evaluate a code-enforced backstop at the releaseTask() choke point in apps/mcp-server/src/interface/mcp/tools/system/coordinationTools.ts (single choke point, also guard task_force_release_orphan) refusing release of task_id matching ^published: . Prefer a task_id-prefix guard over a new task_kind enum value: published: markers and cron: election locks TODAY share task_kind cowork-slot with opposite semantics (dispatch-claim SKILL.md §3.1 table literally documents TTL never released vs explicit release at dispatch end for the same kind), and adding an enum member has a known drift class (feedback_preclaim_gate_taskkind_enum_drift: Zod enum + SQLite CHECK + call sites). ALSO IN SCOPE: chef.md Step 0.5 omits owner_client_session entirely — a violation of spawn-fanout.md L56 (REQUIRED, P1-FINAL TASK_1980) and an unfixed repeat of 07-03 defect #2. AC: (1) invariant holds for both single-fire (TTL 100800) and multi-fire (TTL=cadence) slots; (2) a silent/no-post exit leaves NO marker; (3) a successful publish leaves a marker no agent can release; (4) all 6 copy-pasted gates wired to the one skill; (5) RAW-verify via task_list_held after a real evening dish — marker MUST still be held.

backlog.title: cowork last_fired is bumped on spawn DISPATCH-success, not delivery proof -> a spawn that dies before writing its notebook still satisfies the cadence gate -> genuine slot misses are MASKED (matcher never re-offers)
backlog.note:
[po 2026-07-21T21:0xZ — FOLD-IN of TNB c115 finding F-COWORK-SCHEDULE-CHEFEVENING-LASTFIRED-STALE. FACT CONFIRMED, TNB'S DIAGNOSIS REFUTED, NO NEW ROW MINTED — this row already owns the correct fix.]

THE FACT (PO verified live): docs/data/cowork-schedule.json slot chef-evening (cron "45 19 * * *") has last_fired = 2026-07-19T19:50:29.901Z — stale by 2 days. The other three chef slots updated correctly to 07-21 (chef-morning 05:19:18Z, chef-intraday 08:19:18Z, chef-eod 08:49:11Z). A real chef-evening fire on 07-21 IS attested: docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-21-evening.json exists with metadata.cycle_id "evening-2026-07-21T19:51:23Z".

TNB'S DIAGNOSIS IS WRONG AND MUST NOT BE CARRIED FORWARD. TNB concluded "dispatcher/scheduler-side metadata bug ... recommend agent-father/ops investigate why only this one slot's last_fired write isn't landing." PO refutes: the write did not FAIL — it never RAN, and for two different reasons across the two stale days. Neither is a failing write, so an investigation into "why the write isn't landing" would search for a bug that does not exist.
  - 2026-07-20: chef-evening genuinely did NOT fire. docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-2026-07-20-evening.json does not exist (PO ls-confirmed; TNB's own GAP-CHEF-SYNTHESIS-A finding independently reports it absent). last_fired correctly did not advance. Real miss, correctly recorded.
  - 2026-07-21: chef-evening DID fire, but NOT via the cowork dispatcher. Commit 62cf2eab8 ("chore(cowork-team): tick 19:45Z HELD — peer router pre-dispatched chef-evening") states it exactly: "Spawn skipped: peer session held published:chef-evening:2026-07-21 78s before this dispatcher won its fire-time election. Instance 4 of the router-intent/cowork-election namespace split." The cowork dispatcher deliberately HELD and never spawned; last_fired is written ONLY on the cowork dispatch path; so it was never touched. The dish was produced by the router path, which does not write last_fired at all.
  => stale-since-07-19 = (07-20 genuine miss) + (07-21 router-path fire). Two causes, one symptom, zero failing writes.

WHY THIS BELONGS ON THIS ROW AND NOT A NEW ONE: this row's thesis is "last_fired is bumped on spawn DISPATCH-success, not delivery proof". The chef-evening case is the SAME root statement observed in the OPPOSITE DIRECTION, and that direction is not yet written down here:
  - Direction already captured: dispatch succeeded, delivery did not => a dead spawn still satisfies the cadence gate => genuine misses are MASKED (matcher never re-offers).
  - Direction added now: delivery succeeded, cowork-path dispatch did not => a real, published dish leaves last_fired stale => a FALSE MISS is fabricated, and any coverage audit trusting cowork-schedule.json as ground truth concludes 2 consecutive missed fires that never happened. TNB's c115 nearly did exactly that.
  Both directions have ONE fix, which is this row's existing fix: bind last_fired to DELIVERY PROOF rather than to the dispatcher's own spawn action. Under that fix the 07-21 router-path fire bumps last_fired (delivery proof exists: synthesis JSON + notebook), and the 07-20 miss still does not. Both cases become correct simultaneously. No second row is needed and a second row would fragment one fix across two owners.

SCOPE CONSEQUENCE — READ BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: the fix must NOT be implemented as "also bump last_fired on the router dispatch path". That merely adds a second writer of the same dispatch-shaped signal and re-creates the masking direction on a new path. The delivery-proof source must be an artifact the SLOT produces (synthesis JSON / notebook / published marker), read independently of WHICH path spawned the agent. Path-agnostic by construction.

CROSS-REF: FIX-COWORK-DISPATCH-ROUTER-INTENT-MUTEX-BYPASS (P0, occ=3). The 07-21 chef-evening event is instance 4 of that class and, per the commit, the first captured with all locks still live. Note for that row: this is its first observed DATA-CORRUPTION consequence — previously it was tracked purely as a double-dispatch/double-publish risk; here the guard WORKED (inner marker gate held, no double publish) and the residue was silent corruption of cadence telemetry. A caught instance is not a harmless instance.
EVIDENCE UPGRADE: this row was minted on reasoning about the masking direction. It now has a live, RAW-verified, 2-day instance with a commit-attested cause. AC should require a negative control (a genuine miss must still leave last_fired unadvanced) so the fix is not just "always bump".

backlog.router_shipped_arm_never_worked_20260721: THE SEVERE FINDING NEITHER ROUTER NOR PO HAD BEFORE THIS PASS: THE ALREADY-SHIPPED WEEKEND ARM HAS NEVER WORKED AT REAL CADENCE. backlog.title: Router demand-dispatch of cowork slots is slot-tick-blind — intent: PRE-CLAIM grants false exclusivity; probe published:<slot>:<period> before spawn + never override a spawned agent window guard
backlog.note: MINTED 2026-07-15T20:06Z by po from signal cow-20260715T195545. Hole 2 of 2 (hole 1 = UC-CCA-P3 marker lifecycle, P0). DEFENCE-IN-DEPTH, NOT the root cause: with a correct marker gate the 19:53Z router-spawned chef would have hit claimed:false and exited, so UC-CCA-P3 alone closes the double-publish. This row stops the wasted expensive run and the false-exclusivity signal. (1) NAMESPACE BLINDNESS: router Phase B PRE-CLAIM (CLAUDE.md §2.5) claims intent:<agent>:<intent-key>, a namespace disjoint from the cowork dispatcher cron:<flow>:<tick> election AND from its per-slot cowork-slot claims. claimed:true on an intent: key says NOTHING about whether that slot already fired this period — at 19:53Z it returned claimed:true while the 19:45Z tick had already published id 932. Fix: before demand-dispatching ANY cowork slot (unified-agent/chef, fb-market-poster, digest-predict, alert-commander, market-watcher), probe READ-ONLY task_list_held for published:<slot>:<period> and check git log for a recent chore(cowork): <slot> tick FIRE commit; either present -> report slot already fired at HH:MMZ and STOP without spawning. Read-only probe only — the router must NOT claim or release the publish marker. (2) OPERATOR FACTOR — DISCLOSED, NOT SUPPRESSED: the router spawned CHEF with do NOT re-derive the window and do NOT exit as outside-window, which disabled main.md outside-window EXIT. At 19:53Z (evening window 19:37 UTC) that guard would have caught the late invocation and prevented publish 933. It was the LAST layer still functioning and the router removed it. Rule to encode: an explicit user slot= request is a request to RUN the slot, not a licence to bypass slot dedup or window guards; NEVER instruct a spawned agent to skip a window/date guard; the guard would have stopped me is the guard WORKING. Off-window demand runs need PO authorisation, not router improvisation. Publishes are irreversible — a skipped dish is recoverable, a double post is not. Files: CLAUDE.md §2.5, .claude/skills/dispatch-claim/SKILL.md (§3.1 namespace table already documents the published/cron distinction but nothing makes the router consult it), .claude/skills/dispatch/SKILL.md. Lesson already in memory: feedback_router_demand_dispatch_cowork_slot_double_publish. AC: (1) router demand-dispatch of an already-fired slot STOPS without spawning and reports the prior fire time; (2) no router path instructs an agent to bypass a window/date guard; (3) probe is read-only — RAW-verify the marker is untouched after a blocked demand-dispatch.

backlog.po_vocabulary_evidence: HARD EVIDENCE FOUND BY po 2026-07-21T19:29:49Z — the status vocabulary is ALREADY fragmented in live data, which makes this row concrete rather than theoretical. .claude/skills/signal-dashboard/SKILL.md is the SSOT and defines exactly three transitions: NEW -> READ (ACK, line 80) -> RESOLVED (CLOSE, line 81), with PRUNE at line 90 evicting rows whose 'status IN (READ, RESOLVED, SUPERSEDED) AND ts older than 24h'. But a census of .signal_queue.rows[] returns: 73 rows status='triaged', 9 status='NEW', 1 status='RETRACTED'. NEITHER 'triaged' NOR 'RETRACTED' appears anywhere in the skill's vocabulary. CONSEQUENCE: because the PRUNE predicate matches only READ/RESOLVED/SUPERSEDED, all 73 'triaged' rows are structurally unprunable and accumulate in the hot file forever — a permanently growing hot-file cost with no eviction path. This is a second, independent failure mode of the same missing contract, and it is not the one the escalation raised. po deliberately used the canonical 'RESOLVED' token for this cycle's 8 rows rather than perpetuating 'triaged'.

backlog.note:
MINTED 2026-07-15 by po from signal cow-20260715T212838 (data-integrity, MED). ROOT CAUSE: signal/synthesis filenames carry ticker+date+mode (or date_vn+dish_type) with NO cycle discriminator; bctc-analyst runs 4x/day (cron 0 15,18,21,0 UTC) so all 4 cycles collide on the same path (39 such filenames in processed/). HARM (the real one, not the lost artifact): the drain READS these files to route signals; if cycle N writes the same filename as cycle N-1 between drains, N silently destroys N-1's UNROUTED signal and it is never triaged. Today the hourly drain interleaved so nothing was lost -- luck, not a guard; a late/missed drain loses a signal silently. 3 INSTANCES SAME CLASS SAME DAY: (1) chef synthesis date_vn+dish_type -> run2 clobbered run1 (Write, silent); (2) tnb notebook same collision, caught ONLY by the Edit tool stale-read check; (3) bctc signals ticker+date+mode -> 9240 overwritten by 8120. feedback_recurring_bug_escalation (2+ -> block) qualifies. SAME ONE-LINE FIX EACH TIME: key the filename by cycle_id (bctc already carries one; chef's is already in metadata). SCOPE (ba/architect own HOW): the docs/signals/*.json writers (bctc-analyst, chef/unified-agent, tnb) + docs/data/unified-agent-synthesis-<DATE>-<SLOT>.json + the Signal Bus naming contract docs/standards/mcp-tools.md (Naming Contract) + the drain reader that consumes filenames. DISTINCT-FROM (checked, none cover this): FU-CTG-DISCOVERY-FILENAME-FILTER (VPS HNX discovery CV_CBTT filename detection), FU-BACKFILL-REAL-FILENAMES (backfill real-filename heuristic), FIX-COWORK-SCHEDULE-STALE-BASE-CLOBBER. OBSERVATION folded (mechanism UNPROVEN -- do NOT diagnose, NOT a blocker): signal_id regressed 9240->8120 over 20h same file/tool/sequence; parsimonious candidate = SQLite INTEGER PRIMARY KEY WITHOUT AUTOINCREMENT reuses max(rowid)+1 after the drain prunes highest rows; NOT probed because the LIVE DB is a named volume, not docs/signals/signals.db (feedback_live_db_is_named_volume_not_host_data); cheap check for the implementer = does the SERVING schema use AUTOINCREMENT. If ids ARE reused, any cross-time signal_id reference can silently re-bind to an unrelated later signal (worse than an orphan FK -- looks resolved). AC: (1) two same-day cycles for the same ticker/mode never share a signal/synthesis path; (2) a between-drains double-write of the same ticker+date+mode cannot silently destroy an unrouted signal; (3) the drain-reader change (if any) preserves routing of both cycles' signals.

backlog.note: Split out of FIX-COMMIT-PATH-PEER-INDEX-SWEEP-GUARD architect design (docs/architecture-briefs/2026-07-21-commit-path-peer-index-sweep-guard.md § AC-6). The commit-path pre-commit hook detects a sweep from the SWEEPING actor's own process at commit time (git diff --cached is race-free once inside the hook's index.lock transaction) but git carries NO per-file staging-intent attribution, so the SWEPT victim (who never gets to run a commit at all -- its git add just silently loses the race) cannot be notified in real time by anything living on the commit path alone. backlog.po_addendum_20260721T1640_EXISTING_CONTR: MATERIAL for the design — read `.claude/skills/commit-mutex/SKILL.md` before designing anything new. A control for this exact race ALREADY EXISTS and the fix may be to close its bypass rather than invent a second mechanism. Three findings, raw-read from the skill 2026-07-21T16:40Z: (1) PURPOSE line states verbatim that it exists to 'eliminate the verify->commit race on the shared git index' — so this defect class was already identified and a mutex shipped for it. (2) The skill is DISPATCHER-ONLY by INV-GATEWAY-1 (specialists lack the gateway binding for task_claim and are told to 'commit directly (explicit paths)'). So a large set of actors is architecturally EXEMPT from the only existing control, and any actor not holding the mutex races freely against one that does — a mutex only excludes participants. Worth checking whether the three sweeping actors (system-auditor, router, cowork-team) held it; the sweeps suggest not. (3) The skill's OWN critical section encodes the defective idiom: Step 3a `git add <paths>`, Step 3b a `git diff --cached --name-only` foreign-path check, Step 3c a BARE `git commit -m` with no pathspecs. Step 3b is precisely the snapshot-not-a-lock check that demonstrably failed the cowork-team actor in 0e28eed23. Under a correctly-held mutex 3b/3c is mostly safe; against a non-participating peer it is not. STRICTLY BETTER and already mandated by CLAUDE.md + the pathspec-commit memory: pathspec-scoped `git commit -m <msg> -- <paths>`, which resolves the paths atomically at commit time instead of trusting a prior index snapshot. Architect should decide whether the deliverable is (i) a new hook, (ii) fixing Step 3c to a pathspec commit plus widening mutex participation, or (iii) both — but note that (ii) alone remains vigilance-shaped (it is still a doc that actors must choose to follow), which is the failure mode this row exists to end. backlog.title: An agent-side context-budget limit is written into permanent report state as a data failure — failed_ct is indistinguishable between 'source data is bad' and 'worker could not hold a 1.2MB image'
backlog.mechanism: For the final 4 windows of POW_2026_Q1 the refine agent reported the page-28 image fetch returned ~1.2MB of base64 that 'exceeded context token budget'. That is a limit of the SUBAGENT's context window — not a property of the document and not of the pipeline. Per its error-boundary contract the agent pushed FAILED for those windows and called finalize_bctc_refine, producing refine_status=FAILED with failed_ct=28.
backlog.why_it_matters: The failure reason is now indistinguishable, in stored state, from a genuine data defect. A future remediation pass reading failed_ct=28 cannot tell that some windows failed because a transcription worker could not hold a 1.2MB image rather than because the page is unreadable. Combined with the head-of-line row this is also what makes the head row PERMANENTLY dead: the finalization is sticky.
backlog.fix_direction: Introduce a distinct terminal-ish status (e.g. DEFERRED / RESOURCE_EXCEEDED) that does NOT finalize the report and leaves the window re-attemptable by a worker with a larger budget or via an image-downscale path. Do not class it with text_fetch_failed.
backlog.scoping_caution: The agent FOLLOWED its documented graceful-degradation contract — this is NOT filed as agent misbehaviour. The defect is that the contract has no distinct terminal status for 'worker could not process within its own resource envelope' versus 'source data is bad'. Prior art (the BCTC reingest guard: 56/56 FAILED/empty-markdown, data-loss guard refused to wipe bctc_table_rows) shows the downstream cost of that ambiguity is already being paid elsewhere.
backlog.advisory_do_not_chase: The refine agent recommended 'investigate upstream text extraction (get_bctc_page_text) for POW reports'. That is WRONG-ROOTED as a current root cause and must not become a task: the store reports text_status=COMPLETE, cowork-team called get_bctc_page_text(report_id=78b06684..., page_number=1) — one of the 24 pages said to have failed — and got full Vietnamese OCR text with source='sqlite_ocr', and the agent's own report contradicts itself ('Page 28 text retrieved successfully'). LIMIT ON THIS REFUTATION: it does NOT prove text was retrievable when the 24 units failed on 2026-07-19; text may have been backfilled since. It establishes only that pointing an implementer at get_bctc_page_text TODAY sends them at a component that demonstrably works.

backlog.title: news-chain BCTC fallback writes an all-zeros balance sheet into financial_reports — the authoritative table — where it is byte-indistinguishable from OCR corruption at serve time; decide whether it should write there AT ALL before guarding arm (b2)
backlog.origin: QA found this sibling writer while approving arm (b2) on parseBctcReport.ts::storeReport(), and explicitly DECLINED to mint or to expand that row (correctly — PO had a scope-hold on it). Router sharpened the finding at source and also declined to mint. Minting is PO's; this is that mint.
backlog.mechanism: newsChainFallback.ts (apps/mcp-server/src/application/usecases/bctc/newsChainFallback.ts) is a SECOND, independently-implemented writer to the same financial_reports (action_code, sort_key) row as storeReport(). It already has arm (b1): lines 264-274 block the write when existingReportRow.total_assets > 0, preserving a previously-good row and logging BLOCKED. What it LACKS is arm (b2): with NO prior row it proceeds to INSERT a brand-new row whose totalAssets is a hardcoded 0 (line 307, bound into the INSERT at line 535), inside an entire all-zeros balance sheet at lines 304-313. Identical defect shape to the one just fixed in storeReport(): refuses to overwrite a good row, but freely CREATES a fresh zero-total row that bctcIdentityGuard.ts then reads at serve time as the OCR-corruption fingerprint. The file's own comment at lines 254-263 already says it 'carried the same two defects' and 'mirrors the identical guard' — the mirror was completed for only one of the two arms.
backlog.po_verified_at_source_20260721T1811: PO RE-READ THE FILE THIS TICK rather than accepting QA's or router's description, and the single decisive fact checks out: `totalAssets: 0` at line 307 is a hardcoded LITERAL and is the ONLY assignment to that field in the whole file (grep: refs at 73, 255, 307, 425, 535 — 307 is the sole write, 535 binds it to the INSERT, 425 is the SQL column list, 255 is the comment, 73 is the summary formatter). There is NO code path in this function that can produce a non-zero balance sheet. The surrounding lines 304-313 are likewise all-zero literals across currentAssets, nonCurrentAssets, liabilities, equity and totalLiabilitiesAndEquity.
backlog.product_question_decide_before_scoping: ANSWER THIS FIRST — the fix does not follow from the defect. Question as router framed it: if a news-inference fallback only ever produces directional hints and never real balance-sheet figures, is writing it into financial_reports — the table bctcIdentityGuard treats as authoritative at serve time — the actual design error, such that guarding arm (b2) alone merely relocates the problem? PO'S STRONG STEER, WITH THE PROOF: YES, IT IS THE DESIGN ERROR, and here is the reductio that settles it. Arm (b1) already blocks every write where a good row exists. Arm (b2), applied literally, blocks every write where NO row exists AND totalAssets<=0. Since totalAssets is hardcoded 0 on EVERY call (verified above — no path produces otherwise), the two arms together block 100% of this function's writes. Adding arm (b2) does not fix the function; it silently converts it into a total no-op while leaving ~600 lines of live, tested, maintained code in place pretending to be a working fallback. A guard that makes its own subject unreachable is not a guard — it is proof that the write target is wrong. CORROBORATING, AND THE PART THAT MAKES THIS USER-FACING RATHER THAN MERELY UNTIDY: (i) the code's OWN comment at lines 254-259 already concedes the whole argument — 'this fallback ALWAYS writes totalAssets=0 ... it reconstructs directional hints from news signals, never real balance-sheet figures — i.e. every call is, by construction, the exact OCR-corruption fingerprint bctcIdentityGuard.ts checks for at serve time.' The codebase has already diagnosed itself; nobody drew the conclusion. (ii) The write is strictly WORSE than not writing, because it destroys an honest signal: an absent row serves 'Chua co du lieu BCTC' ('we do not have this'), whereas a zeros row serves '[CORRUPT DATA - SKIP] total_assets=0 (OCR extraction failure)' — a false claim that we HAVE the filing and it is broken, which misattributes a defect to the filer. This is the same family of harm as the ngay_nop flip on the parent row: fabricating a state that defames a real-world filing. (iii) buildAnalysisSummary() at line 73 formats this into Vietnamese RAG-retrievable prose — 'Tong tai san: 0 trieu dong.' — a flat factual assertion that the company has zero total assets, written into the retrieval corpus. That is fabricated financial data in a served surface, and it engages feedback_no_fake_data_real_fetch directly. backlog.title: Session-scoped CronCreate loops are invisible and unpersisted across 5 CLI sessions — build the launchd-hosted liveness watchdog that turns 'a session died and its whole loop vanished' from silent into a BUG-channel alert
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 4 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 (cron-registry.json) landing first; this row is that registry's first consumer. See po_design_ruling below: the design call was made, this row implements one third of it.
backlog.problem: CronList in the router session returns 'No scheduled jobs.' Crons live inside 5 separate CLI sessions (dev-team, cowork, system-audit, claude-heler, workflows-fix). No session can see or repair another's crons. When a session dies its whole loop vanishes with zero trace. CronCreate additionally only fires while the REPL is idle, so a session stuck mid-query fires nothing. PO verified there is NO on-disk cron persistence under ~/.claude (no crons dir; ~/.claude/jobs/ holds two stale June background-job state dirs, unrelated).
backlog.po_design_ruling: OPTION (a) BROADER LAUNCHD COVERAGE — SCOPED, plus (c) MONITORING. Option (b), a persistence/registry layer for CronCreate, is REJECTED as a new scheduler. Reasoning: (1) building persistence for CronCreate means re-implementing a scheduler we do not own, inside a surface (the CLI REPL) whose contract can change under us; we already own two durable planes (launchd, and the containerized mcp-server node-cron scheduler with 85 jobs) and a third home-grown one is exactly the 'duplicating cron hosts' that UC-CDC-P5 already names as the thing to avoid. (2) launchd is the ONLY plane that survives session death and it demonstrably works (firer: 815 runs). (3) But WHOLESALE migration to launchd is equally wrong — `claude -p` per tick is expensive and, per FIX-GUARANTEED-SLOT-FIRER-FANOUT-TRUNCATION, structurally truncates fan-out work. (4) The REPL-idle constraint is unfixable from our side; that is a second independent argument for making session-plane failures VISIBLE rather than trying to make the session plane reliable. backlog.title: Three time bases coexist in one scheduling system: server jobs mix timezone UTC and Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh, CronCreate fires at MACHINE-LOCAL France time (CEST/CET, DST-sensitive), and the market it serves is fixed UTC+7 — no single place states what any job's real wall-clock is
backlog.status_note: PO SEQUENCE RANK 7 — gated on UC-SDF-P6 cron-registry.json. A registry that records each job's declared time base is most of this answer; doing it before the registry means writing the same table twice.
backlog.problem: (1) mcp-server scheduler jobs individually declare timezone:'UTC' or timezone:'Asia/Ho_Chi_Minh'. (2) CronCreate jobs fire at machine-local France time (CEST=UTC+2 summer / CET=UTC+1 winter) and therefore SHIFT BY AN HOUR twice a year against the market. (3) Vietnam is fixed UTC+7 with no DST. A job authored as '15:00' has three different meanings depending on which plane it lands on, and nothing declares which.
backlog.dst_is_the_sharp_edge: The France planes silently re-time relative to the VN trading session at each DST transition. docs/standards/cron-jobs.md:292 already documents this reasoning for the guaranteed-slot firer (StartInterval chosen over StartCalendarInterval precisely because the latter is DST-sensitive) — the insight exists but is applied in exactly one place. Next transitions to check against: late Oct 2026 (CEST->CET) shifts every session-plane cron one hour LATER relative to UTC/VN.
backlog.folded_item_5b_minute_collision: FOLDED (item 5b, LOW): restartCadenceAlert (server plane) and cron-db-data-integrity (terminal/session plane) both sit on `15,45 * * * *`. PO assessment: these run in different processes and share no resource except SQLite, so this is a same-minute COINCIDENCE, not a contention bug — it is folded here rather than minted separately because a cron-registry with declared time bases is what makes cross-plane minute maps computable at all, instead of discoverable only by hand-audit.
backlog.explicitly_out_of_scope_verified_good: The auditor :00/:30 vs dev-team :07/:37 vs db-integrity :15/:45 offsets are CORRECT and deliberate. Do NOT 'fix', 'normalize' or 'align' them. Any change that collapses those offsets is a regression.

ready.question: Which other count-threshold gates across flows, scripts and crons are evaluated against an input with a structural floor at or above their threshold, so that they fire unconditionally and can no longer detect the condition they exist to detect?

A threshold whose input has a floor above it is strictly WORSE than no gate: it is false assurance, and it reports success every time it fires.

FIX SHAPE (PO directive): the verdict gate must be a DETERMINISTIC ASSERTION, not a narrative self-judgement. Before writing metadata.quality_verdict="full", the agent must assert per-layer that the layer's own payload field is non-empty AND contains its mandatory tokens (L2: PMI and/or EFFR-IORB). If an assertion fails, "full" is not writable — the verdict must downgrade to "degraded" and a [gap:L<N>_...] token must be appended to known_gaps. Verdict and gap-token must be derived from ONE evaluation so they cannot disagree.

AC: (1) quality_verdict="full" is unwritable when any mandatory layer field lacks its required tokens; (2) verdict and known_gaps are computed from a single pass (no independent second judgement); (3) negative control — a synthetic dish with L2 stripped must produce degraded + an L2 gap token, proving the assertion fires (without this the fix is indistinguishable from always writing degraded); (4) RAW-verify on the next morning fire by reading metadata.quality_verdict + tnb_synthesis.us_macro_layer from the persisted JSON — an agent self-report or notebook line is NOT acceptable evidence (the 07-21 morning notebook line matched the false "full" verbatim, so the notebook faithfully reproduces the bad verdict and cannot detect it).

SIBLING / DO NOT MERGE: FIX-CHEF-L6-TOKEN-PERSISTENCE-RECURRING (P3, BLOCKED) is the nearest prior art and is RELATED BUT DISTINCT. That row = a token WAS generated and then dropped on JSON write (persist-step vs narrative-gen, isolation-first, 3 manifestations despite 2 auto-cures). THIS row = no token was ever generated AND the verdict was affirmatively certified "full". Different mechanism, opposite end of the pipeline. They share the family "chef self-scoring integrity" and should be looked at together, but merging them would bury a false-certification bug inside a persistence bug. The L6 row's own lesson applies here though: more same-shape auto-cure is the wrong move; this needs a deterministic assertion.
